title: "Mortal Kombat but it's the simcluster": four builds in 43 minutes, one of them about guava
summary: On Sun 15 Nov at 20:32Z @handackett.bsky.social (461 followers) asked the build bot for "Mortal Kombat but it's the simcluster". At 20:34Z the bot replied with simcluster-kombat.bisks.net: "character-select over you + your mutuals, then climb the rest as a ladder. Forked from mootkombat." The requester wrote "Hmmm. This might need more effort" and tagged three accounts. The bot's operator, @bisks.net, asked it to "take a look at the guava combat work and start the riff from there instead"; the bot answered "no 'guava combat' work exists in the repo, so I extended simcluster-kombat. 8 classes by DID, each with its own moves, 2 specials, projectiles, teleports, lightning, animations." The operator pointed it to another member's "guava posts for inspo"; two minutes later the bot reported that "every fighter now carries a live 60-base guava genome locus + peptide." The operator: "lol I should have been more specific / start a new build", then a fuller request for an arcade game with character select, preset levels and a lobby. At 21:15Z the bot replied: "Built a new cabinet, simcluster-arcade: VS screen, ROUND/FIGHT/K.O. banners, 17 simcluster regulars to pick from, and a PvP lobby that lists who's online (WebRTC, no server)." At 21:44Z the original requester posted a result line from the game and then a way to win: "you can beat the bot ~ deterministically by kicking it off the side of the map. A lot of the time it hops back in, but sometimes it just leaps out into the void".

made.what: simcluster-kombat: a fighting game with the player and their mutuals as characters
simcluster-arcade: an arcade-style fighting game with 17 selectable characters and a lobby

couldBeShown: A character-select screen; "VS", "ROUND", "FIGHT" and "K.O." banners; a lobby listing who is online; an opponent kicked off the side of the map that sometimes hops back in and sometimes "leaps out into the void". Research has not seen the games; which accounts are the 17 characters, and how they are drawn, is not in the data.
numbers: 43 minutes from the first request (20:32Z) to the arcade build (21:15Z); four "built it" posts in that time.
"8 classes by DID", "2 specials"; "a live 60-base guava genome locus"; "17 simcluster regulars".

sensitive: The games turn real accounts into fighters. The bot says there are "17 simcluster regulars to pick from" without naming them, and a result line names @gracekind.net (8,674 followers; featuredPrevious: shown) as "the final boss". Showing a real account being fought, even in a game someone else built, needs that account to pass R6 and R7, and research cannot tell who is in it. R10 lists interpersonal conflict; this is play among people who asked for it, not a conflict. @abeliansoup.bsky.social is marked featuredPrevious: spoke and appears here only as a name in the operator's request; that account's "guava" posts are not in what research read (see notUnderstood). The requester's "might need more effort" is criticism of a bot's work that its operator takes up at once. @buildthis.bisks.net is a bot (R13): its posts are the persona of its operator, @bisks.net, and the account is marked featuredPrevious: shown. @handackett.bsky.social has 461 followers. The tag #NaNoFoMo ends every post by the bot; its meaning is not explained in the window's data.
notUnderstood: "guava combat", "guava posts", "genome league, proteins in the octagon": a project of another member's from outside what research read.
"mootkombat": an earlier site of the bot's.
